# Eve

> Eve is a free, MIT-licensed push-to-talk dictation app for Windows. Hold a hotkey and speak; when you stop, Eve pastes the text into the active window. In the packaged app, speech recognition runs in a local service on your machine. Eve is pre-release software; see the latest release for its version and notes.

## What it does

- Hotkeys: Ctrl+Win for quick notes, Ctrl+Shift+Win for long dictation. Hold to talk, or switch to toggle.
- A small translucent pill shows a voice-reactive bead and a timer while you speak, and shrinks to a breathing dot in silence. It shows no transcript. Text is not typed into other apps while you speak.
- Eve copies the final text, pastes it into the active window, and can then restore your previous clipboard.
- Output styles: Raw Dictation pastes what you said. Clean Prompt, Codex Prompt, Message Rewrite, and Command Mode apply local, rule-based cleanup first.
- Hotwords help with names, acronyms, and product terms. History can be searched and exported to JSON or CSV. Insights are calculated locally.
- Speech engine: Faster-Whisper through CTranslate2. Models include large-v3-turbo (recommended, about 1.5 GB), large-v3 (about 2.9 GB, maximum accuracy), and small (about 0.5 GB, lighter hardware).
- New CPU-only profiles start on small for a faster first download. large-v3-turbo runs fastest with the optional GPU pack; the project's CPU tests found it too slow for ordinary short dictation. Existing profiles keep their saved model.

## Install

1. Download Eve.Web.Setup.<version>.exe from GitHub Releases.
2. Run it. It is a small nsis-web installer that downloads the app during setup, so it needs an internet connection. It is unsigned, so Windows SmartScreen may ask you to confirm.
3. Open Eve and hold Ctrl+Win. The speech model downloads from Hugging Face the first time you use it.

Each release publishes SHA256SUMS.txt and SHA512SUMS.txt.

## System requirements

- Windows 10 or 11, x86-64.
- RAM: 4 GB minimum; 8 GB or more recommended.
- Disk: about 686 MB unpacked, measured on a September 2026 build candidate (not a measurement of the latest release). Allow more for speech models and the optional GPU pack.
- Internet for the web installer payload and the first model download.
- Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable. Eve links to the official installer when it is missing.
- No GPU needed.

## Privacy

- In the packaged app, speech recognition runs on your machine. Audio and transcripts are never uploaded.
- No account and no telemetry.
- History and Insights live in a local SQLite database. Long-dictation audio is temporary and is never written to History or logs.
- The network is used to download the installer payload, model weights on first use, and the optional GPU pack if you install it. A developer can also connect to a separately started localhost speech service.
- Copied diagnostics exclude logs, file paths, History, and transcript text. Review any report before sharing it.

## Optional NVIDIA GPU pack

- Eve works on the CPU. The NVIDIA CUDA pack is optional, downloaded separately from Settings, verified by hash, and speeds up transcription on supported GPUs.
- The pinned pack is 494,950,029 bytes compressed and 771,188,224 bytes installed.
- It needs a supported driver and sufficient VRAM. It has not been shown to work on every NVIDIA machine.

## Release status

Eve is pre-release software, so expect rough edges. Read the latest release notes to see what has and has not been verified. No accuracy or latency figures are claimed here.
